description: This topic is a crucial part of India's rich cultural heritage. It includes an exam-oriented classification of the recognized classical dances and traditional folk dances of various Indian states.

sections.title: Fundamentals of Indian Dance Art
sections.description: Important concepts related to the origin and basic components of Indian classical dances.

key_concepts.explanation: An ancient treatise written by Bharat Muni, considered the primary source of all Indian classical dances. It is also referred to as the 'Fifth Veda'.
The masculine and aggressive aspect of dance associated with Lord Shiva, focusing heavily on rhythm and movement.
The gentle and graceful aspect of dance associated with Goddess Parvati, focusing on emotion and expression (Rasa and Bhava).

important_facts.fact: Dances in India are primarily divided into two categories: Classical Dances, which are bound by strict rules, and Folk Dances, which are based on local traditions.

sections.title: Recognized Classical Dances of India
sections.description: The 8 major classical dances of India recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi and their respective states.

key_associations.extra_info: It is the oldest classical dance in India. Rukmini Devi Arundale is its famous exponent.
Based on the stories of Radha-Krishna. Pt. Birju Maharaj was its prominent dancer.
World-famous for its elaborate makeup, masks, and heavy costumes.
The 'Tarangam', performed by dancing on the edges of a brass plate, is its special attraction.
The 'Tribhanga' posture (bending the body at three parts) is the main feature of this dance. Kelucharan Mohapatra is a famous dancer.
Deeply connected to Vaishnavism and Rasleela. The Jhaveri Sisters are famous for it.
A solo dance primarily performed by women, inspired by the Mohini avatar of Lord Vishnu.
Introduced in the 15th century by Saint Srimanta Sankardev in Vaishnavite monasteries.

sections.title: Major Folk Dances of North and West India
sections.description: Traditional dances performed on the occasions of festivals and harvesting in various states of North and West India.

key_associations.extra_info: Primarily performed during the nine-day festival of Navratri.
Kalbelia is also called the 'Snake Charmer Dance' and is included in the UNESCO heritage list.
Bhangra is performed by men and Giddha by women, especially during Baisakhi.
Graceful dances performed by women to celebrate the spring season and harvest.
A highly energetic dance form performed to the beats of the Dholki.
Recorded in the Guinness Book of World Records as the largest folk dance.

sections.title: Major Folk Dances of South, East and Northeast India
sections.description: Important folk dances reflecting the cultural diversity of South India, Eastern states, and the Northeast.

key_associations.extra_info: A traditional theater form that is a rich blend of dance, music, and dialogue.
A fast-paced, joyous dance performed during the spring season and Assamese New Year.
A martial art-based folk dance. It has three types: Seraikella, Mayurbhanj, and Purulia Chhau.
The traditional dance of the Yaduvanshis, specifically performed after Diwali.
Also known as the 'Bamboo Dance', where dancers step between moving bamboo sticks.
A dance performed by women of the Reang tribe, featuring an amazing feat of balancing.

sections.title: Important Facts and Characteristics
sections.description: Some of the most crucial facts and global recognitions related to classical and folk dances.

important_facts.fact: The Ministry of Culture recognizes 'Chhau' as the 9th Classical Dance of India, whereas the Sangeet Natak Akademi considers it a folk dance.
Rajasthan's 'Kalbelia' and Eastern India's 'Chhau' are included in UNESCO's List of Intangible Cultural Heritage.
Gujarat's 'Garba' was recently added to the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in the year 2023.
In classical dances, hand gestures used to express emotions and tell stories are called 'Mudras'.
